content.thinking:
I need to plan the scythe's proportions and pose carefully: roughly 1.9m tall, standing upright on a small pedestal with the shaft vertical and the blade curving forward near the top.

I'll ground it on a round dragonbone plinth with glowing rune rings, then build the shaft as a bone-like structure using cylinders and spheres to mimic vertebrae, with knobby rings and spinous spikes along its length, plus cloth wraps for the grip section.

At the top, I'm designing a dragon skull mount where a claw-like grasp holds a soul orb, and the long curved blade sweeps outward and down from that joint, giving the whole scythe an organic, bone-forged look.

Making the blade bone-white with a thin glowing cyan strip along the inner cutting edge, offsetting those points slightly inward to form a second thinner outline without crossing the main blade shape.

Since the strip overlaps the blade edge only along that boundary line, I'll keep thicknesses slightly different to avoid z-fighting. For blade details I'm adding bone-rib spikes along the outer edge and considering a scale or crack-based cel paint pattern for the bone texture.

I'll use a mottled bone cel paint where the lighting's z-component naturally shades the front face lit and back face shadowed. I also want rune glyph decals on the blade face, done as a transparent textured plane with glowing cyan runes positioned slightly offset in z so they sit just above the blade surface near its midsection.

Working out rune placement...

I'll just use rotation without a separate dir vector, and for the back side I can mirror the plane with a flipped rotation so the rune reads correctly from behind, offsetting it slightly in z. For the glyph texture itself I'm sketching an SVG with glowing cyan strokes on a small viewbox.

Now I'm scaling the stroke thickness for the larger texture size and writing a function to generate four distinct glyph variants, then applying the glow effect to the textured plane part. For the blade's mounting point, I'm positioning a skull between the shaft and blade, figuring out its orientation and scale so the cranium sits naturally where the blade emerges.

Writing skull snout and horn geometry...

Now I'm adding glowing cyan eyes, small downward teeth cones along the snout, a lower jaw frustum, nostrils, and brow spikes. I'm also considering adding a floating soul orb caged in bone ribs lower on the shaft.

I'll skip the uncertain `frame` import and instead build soul wisps as tapered glowing swept tubes trailing downward off the blade's cutting edge, like dripping flame curls. For the base, I'm planning a stepped bone lathe plinth with a rim of small glowing cyan rune plates around it.

For the butt-foot, I'll add three curved claw sweeps gripping the shaft from the plinth upward with tapering radii, keeping the shaft mostly straight but structured in distinct bands going up: claws, vertebrae, a gold ring, cloth wrap with painted stripes, more vertebrae, an orb cage, neck vertebrae, then the skull. I'm now defining the vertebra geometry as a series of small cylinders placed along these y-sections.

Each vertebra gets a flared hourglass-style cylinder in bone color with tiny side prongs alternating left-right-ish in z, and I'm leaving gaps between them to reveal a dark violet rod core running through the shaft. Now I'm sketching a ridge of thicker bone tubes swept along the blade's outer edge, offset slightly inward from the silhouette to create a bulging spine-like structure.

I'm adding barb spikes jutting up from the ridge at several points along its length, and thin curved rib struts running from the ridge down to the inner edge like bone-supported wing membrane, placed symmetrically on both faces of the blade so they stay within its thickness. I'm also finalizing the overall blade thickness and bevel, then setting up the bone color palette.

Now I'm defining the paint shaders: a cel-shaded bone paint with mottled coloring and a derived shadow tone, plus a custom blade paint that uses cellular noise to detect crack lines near the inner edge and renders them as dark fractures over the base bone coloring.

I'm also adding a smoothstep-based gradient toward the tip, shifting from bone to a soul-violet tint, and tightening up imports to only include the modules actually used—THREE, builder/path helpers, paint utilities, and the toon/glow kits.

Now I'm sketching out the build function itself: a default export that constructs the scythe via a builder and returns its root, using a lathe geometry for the plinth base (solid outline from axis to rim, closed loop, 10 segments) topped by the shaft. I'm placing small outward-facing rune plate boxes evenly around the plinth's rim, computing their position with sine/cosine and rotating each to face outward along the radius.

I'm swapping those boxes for glowing textured planes carrying a rune glyph, rotated to face outward and sized to sit flush against the plinth's curved wall. I'm also adding a thin gold torus ring near the top of the plinth for decoration, then laying out the skull geometry -- a scaled sphere for the cranium, an elongated snout box, and an angled frustum box for the lower jaw, positioning each piece relative to a central skull coordinate so the blade appears to emerge naturally from the side of the head.

Now I'm placing the eye sockets as dark hollow spheres with slightly smaller glowing spheres nested just inside them for a faint ember effect, and I'm sketching out curved horn sweeps on either side that arc backward and upward using tapered tube geometry, making sure they stay clear of the blade's path. I'm also planning brow and cheek spikes as short directional cones jutting outward, and starting to lay out a row of upper teeth as small spikes along the lower edge of the snout.

Now I'm computing the underside curve of the snout to position teeth so the upper and lower jaw rows nearly meet in a closed-mouth look, adding tiny nostril dimples near the snout tip, and transitioning to the neck structure -- stacking vertebra segments up to the skull base with a gold collar ring, then designing the soul orb cage with a glowing cyan sphere wrapped in rib-like arcs and capped with gold at top and bottom.

I'm sketching hanging wisp tendrils that dangle from the blade's inner edge, computing curved paths with tapering radii so each wisp trails downward and fades to a point, varying their base positions and lengths along the blade so they feel organic, and alternating their glow color between the soul-cyan and a purple hue for visual variety.

Now I'm adding gold accents: a clasp near the blade root, a banded torus with a small jewel, and gold studs on the skull crown for decorative detail. I'm also adding soul-colored cloth tassels hanging from a ring, then wrapping the shaft with a striped paint pattern using alternating purple and dark indigo bands.

I'm adding a socket collar at the base of the staff and designing a glyph function that generates SVG rune symbols with glowing teal strokes and rounded caps, each glyph variant using a distinct path pattern for a runic texture atlas.

Now I'm calculating the positions, rotations, and glyph indices for runes placed along the blade's curved edge, matching each rune's tilt angle to the local slope of the blade contour so they sit flush against it.

I'm also deciding to drop the strut ribs since they'd collide visually with the rune placements along the blade, and instead refining the blade's root outline near the hilt to extend it slightly back for a more grounded connection to the guard.

I'm working out the glow strip polygon that runs along the blade's inner edge, matching its smoothing curve so the glow traces the blade shape without crossing itself or overlapping the solid body except at the shared boundary, extruded as a thin sheet along the blade's local axes.

Now I'm planning the remaining structural pieces: orb cage ribs with gold cap cylinders top and bottom, a sequence of vertebra-like loops and prongs climbing the shaft, a gold torus ring at the plinth base, and several collar rings along the shaft at different heights — then assembling all of this into the final code.
